newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. says first Rwanda aid plane set to depart.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says first Rwanda aid plane set to depart.

text.p: The United States air force said its first cargo plane bound for Kigali to help in the Rwandan refugee crisis would depart on Tuesday evening.
The aircraft was scheduled to leave Germany for Kigali at 1900 GMT.
"We expect to send part of a tanker air lift control unit to set up the preliminary controls for the region," a spokesman at Rhein-Main air base told Reuters.

The spokesman said the C-17 aircraft was being loaded with equipment to allow U.S. forces to set up an air traffic control system for the Kigali airport. Also being loaded was equipment needed to unload humanitarian supplies on subsequent flights.
"There are no armed troops on the flight to clear the way," he said.

U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said on Tuesday that the United States has changed plans to send security troops to Zaire and instead will provide fewer than 1,000 military logistics personnel to aid refugees in Rwanda.

Perry said that the situation in central Africa remained fluid and, while a Canadian-led multinational force would now operate chiefly in Rwanda, Washington was ready to send protective troops to Zaire if necessary.

The United States was one of the most reluctant volunteers to the U.N.-backed 10,000-strong multinational force whose mission was mainly to help the 1.2 million Rwandan and Burundian Hutus stranded in eastern Zaire by a month-long rebellion.
About 14 countries who committed troops to the force are due to review their plans in Germany on Thursday.
